name: Race-and-panel acceptance: noise-allocated sequential screening with a known-variance confirmation
core_idea: Replace design o's fixed step (1 seed x 4 categories, best half to 2 more seeds, then a t over 16 pairs) with a measurement built from the measured noise and costs. Knapsack is dropped: it has no signal and takes 52% of a step's CPU. Every candidate is then raced on part A of quadratic assignment, job shop and p-median. Runs are allocated in proportion to paired sd / sqrt(CPU), which is 8:3:1 runs per 36-CPU-s cycle (the Neyman allocation for the equal-weight category mean). The race opens with an 8-CPU-s first look and stops by a sequential probability ratio test, so the ~96% of edits that are harmful or slightly harmful are dropped after 50-80 CPU-s on average. The rare survivor is confirmed on a panel of fresh seeds whose parent runs are paid once per parent. The panel adds bin packing, a category that no selection saw, and the test is a known-variance z-test (variance pooled over every lineage and arm) on the registered held-out statistic, min(change of acquired, change of gain), at alpha 0.005 per confirmation. Design o's recursion stays (the parent's own learning principle learns the edit distribution), but it now learns from the race's shrunken estimates instead of one-seed screens. Transfer cannot be certified on four source categories by any acceptance rule, so it is measured directly by re-measuring every accepted step on the held-out categories.
why_it_beats_the_measured_limit:
THE MEASURED LIMIT. The registered confirmation needs a 16-pair mean >= 0.0134 (t >= 2.6 at paired sd 0.021) in its 4-category units. Knapsack's 4 pairs are exact zeros, so this equals 0.0179 on the 3 informative categories (the units used below).

FITTED EFFECT DISTRIBUTION. I fitted a mixture to the brief's facts: screen mean -0.0088, sd 0.0342; correlation 0.10 among promoted candidates; 4 confirmations in 29 steps; +0.0089 shrinking to +0.0012 on confirmation. Script: <scratch>/panel/work/statistics/calib.py. It gives:
- 2% of edits at -0.16 to -0.40;
- 10% at about -0.047;
- the rest at mean -0.008 (pessimistic fit, which matches the 4/29 confirmation share best) to -0.005 (central), sd 0.004-0.005.
Only 0.13% (pessimistic) to 3.6% (central) of candidates are worth >= +0.0039. At those effect sizes the registered rule has <= 5% power.

INFORMATION PER CPU-SECOND (variance x CPU of the 3-category mean):
- registered layout: 0.0071;
- knapsack dropped: 0.0034;
- 8:3:1 allocation: 0.00149, i.e. 4.8x better than registered.
Parent runs on the race pool and the panel are paid once per parent, about another 2x on confirmations. Pooled variances with hundreds of df replace a 15-df t.

CONFIRMATION. 640 CPU-s of candidate runs (QAP 142, JS 53, PM 18 runs, plus a few bin-packing runs) gives SE 0.0015, or 0.0014 with bin packing. Smallest acceptable mean: 2.576 x 0.0015 = 0.0039 (50% power); 80% power at 0.0052. That is 4.6x below the registered 0.0179.

RACE. First look: 8 CPU-s (QAP x2 + JS x1), floor -0.025. Then 36-CPU-s cycles, SE 0.0064 each, testing H0 = 0 against H1 = +0.006 (alpha 0.05, beta 0.2, at most 10 cycles). Mean cost per raced candidate: 54-78 CPU-s.

SIMULATED PER 18,000-CPU-s LINEAGE (40-60 replicates; <scratch>/panel/work/statistics/power.py):

| scenario | race acceptances | registered rule |
|---|---|---|
| pessimistic | 0.2 | ~0.02 |
| central | 3.4 | 0.30 |
| optimistic | 5.2 | 0.37 |

- 92-96% of race acceptances have true effect >= +0.0035; no acceptance with true effect <= 0 was observed.
- CPU per acceptance: ~5,300 (central) and ~90,000 (pessimistic), against ~60,000 and ~900,000 for the registered rule.

FALSE ACCEPTANCE.
- Alpha 0.005 per confirmation by construction.
- Worst-case null (every candidate equal to its parent): 2.7 confirmations and 0.014 expected false acceptances per lineage, about 0.0008 per step. The Bonferroni bound is 0.10 with at most 20 confirmations.
- The registered rule in the same simulation: 0.10 per lineage (its own calibration: 0.108-0.133 per 13 steps).

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. These are source improvements. Let rho be the cross-category correlation of true effects. An accepted edit's expected held-out effect is m + k(x - m), where m ≈ -0.005 (the mean edit), x ≈ +0.007 (its confirmed effect) and k = 3rho/(1+2rho):
- -0.005 at rho 0 (designs a and b measured rho ≈ 0);
- 0.000 at rho 0.2;
- +0.004 at rho 0.5.
More source acceptances therefore help on held-out categories only if rho >= ~0.3. The design measures this through endpoint M3 instead of assuming it.
recursion:
KEPT FROM DESIGN O, UNCHANGED (generation). When a mechanism M* is accepted, the recursive arm rebuilds the discoverer's learner as O.Acquirer(M*, current weights). M*'s live init, propose and update programs then propose the weight vectors over the 43 edit cells and update them from the fitness of the candidates they produced. So a discovered learning principle decides how the next candidates are generated.

CHANGED BY THIS TECHNIQUE (evaluation).
1. The fitness M*'s update program receives is each candidate's race estimate, shrunk toward its arm's running effect distribution. Its reliability among non-harmful candidates is about 0.3-0.8 once a cycle is reached, against about 0.05-0.1 for today's one-seed screen (measured correlation 0.10). The principle learns from signal instead of noise.
2. The race's run allocation and SPRT boundaries for M*'s descendants come from M*'s own paired-noise profile (the pooled noise shrunk toward M*'s measured within-parent variance). A mechanism that acquires more reliably makes every later decision cheaper.

CONTROLS.
- The frozen arm isolates which principle learns. It has the same race, the same common-random-number streams, and generation 0's principle restarted at the same moments.
- A generation test isolates the principle at a fixed parent: 3 replicate pairs from generation 0 at 5,000 CPU-s each, the discovered principle against generation 0's, both learning the weights through the same race. Endpoint: the mean race value of all first-look survivors they generate (about 165 per arm; detectable difference about 0.002), and their harmful share.
- On the held-out categories, the final recursive, frozen and uniform discoverers each draw 120 edits of o0 from their recorded distributions. Each edit is measured once per held-out category on shared seeds, against o0. Detectable: about 0.004 in the trimmed mean effect, 0.009 in the plain mean, and a harmful-share difference of 0.10.

Channel 2 has no separate arm. It is reported as CPU per race decision against the parent's paired variance.

LIKELY OUTCOME. If no principle change is accepted, the recursion is not exercised and the stage records that. This is likely: the principle cells screened between -0.040 and +0.018, with n <= 12 per cell.
mechanism_changes:
UNCHANGED: the kernel (run.py, problem.py, meter, references), design_o.py, edits.py, discovery.py and evaluate.py (raise_until is reused).

NEW rsi6/open/acceptance.py (~300 lines).
- Constants:
  - RACE_CATS = (quadassign, jobshop, pmedian); CLEAN_CAT = binpacking (panel only); DROPPED = knapsack.
  - LOOK0 = {quadassign: 2, jobshop: 1}; LOOK0_FLOOR = -0.025.
  - CYCLE = {quadassign: 8, jobshop: 3, pmedian: 1}, recomputed from the measured sd/sqrt(cpu).
  - THETA1 = 0.006; ALPHA_RACE = 0.05; BETA_RACE = 0.2; MAX_CYCLES = 10.
  - CONF_CPU = 640; Z_CONF = 2.576; MAX_CONF = 20; FUTILITY_AT = 0.5 (non-binding: stop if the estimate is below 0 at half the panel).
  - NOHARM_SE = 2.0 (every category's statistic >= -2 SE); VAR_INFLATE = 1.1; SHRINK_DF = 30; PANEL_REUSE = 4.
- class NoiseModel: pooled paired variance per category over every recorded candidate-parent pair of every lineage and arm (design o's ledger included), per-parent shrinkage, and per-category CPU per run.
- neyman(sd, cpu, total): runs per category.
- stat_G(cand, parent): per category, min(mean change of acquired, mean change of gain).
- class Race(measure, noise).run(candidate, parent, pool): returns {decision, looks, llr, estimate, var, runs, cpu}.
- confirm(measure, noise, candidate, parent, panel, alpha): returns {passed, z, per_category, cpu_ratio}. The variance per category is max(1.1 x pooled, own).
- posterior(est, var, prior).

NEW rsi6/open/discovery_r.py (~280 lines, a fork of discovery.Lineage).
- Race-pool seeds are keyed by the parent's behaviour, so every lineage with that parent shares the runs through the cache.
- Panel seeds are per (arm, lineage, parent index).
- step(): propose kd = 6 as in design o; race each; call D.learn on the posterior values (design o's floor for capped candidates); confirm the best race-passer; accept and rebuild as in design o.
- Records r_race, r_confirm, r_step and r_accept through append_once. The caps CPU_RATIO 1.25 (race) and CPU_STEP 1.10 (panel) are kept.

NEW rsi6/open/experiment_r.py (~300 lines, a fork of experiment_q.py). Stages: discovery, selection, generation (the swap test), heldout (finals, other lineages, o0, a0, raise_until controls, accepted steps, held-out generation test).

ALSO NEW: rsi6/registry/registration_r.json plus an amendment record; rsi6/tests/test_acceptance.py (~150 lines); rsi6/open/diagnose_r.py (~120 lines: rho-hat from off-diagonal covariances, the noise model, race costs, the winner's-curse check).
measurement_design:
ARMS. Common random numbers: lineage k of every arm draws the same stream, as in registration_o. All three arms use the race-and-panel rule; 3 lineages each; 18,000 CPU-s charged per lineage under design o's charging rule and caps.
- R, recursive: the parent's principle learns the edit weights.
- F, frozen: generation 0's principle learns them.
- T, tune: constants and numbers only, drawn uniformly.
The uniform and shuffled discovery arms are dropped; uniform appears only as a generator in the held-out generation test.

CATEGORIES.
- Race: quadassign, jobshop and pmedian (part A). The panel adds binpacking (part A).
- Dropped or excluded:
  - knapsack: the same acquired score for every mechanism;
  - forecasting and regression: prediction form, which design o does not open;
  - partitioning and setcover: 100-300 CPU-s per run; setcover run sd 0.18.
- Held-out: single-machine weighted tardiness, UBQP, RCPSP and maximum clique, touched only by the held-out stage.

BUDGETS.
- Discovery uses registration_o's search budget (train 40, n_train 12, part A). Exception, pre-registered: if budget_scaling.json (development, source only) shows that (sd of edit effects)^2 / (paired variance x CPU) at train 200 is >= 1.5x its value at 40, train 200 is used.
- The held-out stage uses the run budget (n_train 16, both halves).

SEEDS (new ranges, none used before):
- race pools: 2,000,000 + 1,000 x (crc32(behaviour) mod 997) + j;
- panels: 3,000,000 + 100,000 x arm + 10,000 x lineage + 500 x parent index + j;
- selection: 220,001-220,004;
- generation test: 230,000+;
- held-out: 270,001-270,012;
- held-out generation test: 280,001-280,012.

SELECTION. Finals and o0 on part B of the four source categories.

CONTROLS. o0, a0, F-final and T-final each have their training budget raised until they reach R-final's CPU, pair by pair, with registration_o's void rules. The other lineages are measured unmatched, to show the spread.

ENDPOINTS.
- E1: held-out R minus o0@R >= 0.01, with a category-and-seed bootstrap interval excluding 0, not void.
- E2: R minus T@R and R minus F@R, with intervals.
- E3: (a) a principle change is accepted and present in R's final; (b) R minus F@R > 0; (c) generation test: discovered principle minus generation 0's principle in mean race value > 0, 95% interval excluding 0.
- M1: acceptances per lineage and per CPU-second, reported against design o's running experiment.
- M2: null calibration by stub, and confirmed value against part B.
- M3: transfer per accepted step. Every accepted parent-to-child step of every lineage is re-measured on the 4 held-out categories x 6 seeds, paired; the pooled mean is reported with a 95% interval (SE 0.0008-0.003).
- M4: rho-hat.

SUCCESS. Recursive improvement is reported only if E1, E3(a), E3(b) and E3(c) all hold and M3's lower bound is above 0. Anything less is reported as measured.
predictions: Null calibration (stub resampling design o's recorded confirmation pairs with category means removed; every candidate equal to its parent): 0.005 false acceptances per confirmation and 0.014 per 18,000-CPU-s lineage (registered bound 0.10). Design o's rule gives 0.10 per lineage in the same stub.
Acceptances per race lineage, mean over the 9 lineages: 1.0 (expected range 0.2 to 3.4, from the pessimistic to the central fit). At least one acceptance in at least 2 of the 9 lineages.
Race cost: mean 50-80 CPU-s per raced candidate; at least 80% of candidates stopped within 80 CPU-s; at most 5% reach a panel.
Accepted mechanisms' confirmed source statistic: mean +0.006 to +0.008. In the selection stage, each accepting lineage's final beats o0 on part B by at least half the sum of its confirmed steps.
rho-hat (cross-category correlation of true effects among candidates of the mild cells: scalar, theta, update, pick term and cross): at most 0.3, point 0.1.
M3, transfer per accepted step on the held-out categories: pooled mean between -0.006 and +0.002 (point -0.002). If at least 10 steps were accepted, its 95% interval excludes +0.004.
E3(a) not met in at least 2 of the 3 recursive lineages, so E3 fails.
The tune arm accepts at least as many mechanisms as the recursive arm. The mildly positive screens were numeric cells: batch +0.0045, theta perturb +0.003.
Held-out generation test: the learned discoverers (R, F) have a harmful share (held-out effect below -0.02) at least 0.10 below uniform's. R minus F mean effect within +-0.004.
M1: acceptances per CPU-second at least 5x those of design o's registered lineages.
failure_modes: The pessimistic fit holds; it is the one that matches 4 confirmations in 29 steps. About 0.2 acceptances per lineage, most lineages accept nothing, and E1 and E3 fail. The result is a quantified negative (no edit among ~2,700 raced had a confirmed effect >= ~0.005), not a demonstration.

rho ≈ 0, as in designs a and b. Source acceptances do not transfer, and each accepted step is worth about -0.005 (the mean edit) on held-out categories, so more acceptances can lower held-out scores. M3 shows it. No rule on 4 source categories prevents this; only more source categories shrink the category-specific term (for example the six sealed ones, once their test has run).

Candidate-dependent noise (an edit that makes acquisition noisier) would let the pooled variance understate the truth. Mitigated by taking max(1.1 x pooled, own sample variance) and checked by the resampling calibration.
Exact zeros and catastrophic tails make the paired differences non-normal. This shifts the SPRT's error rates, which costs only efficiency; the panel's ~200 runs make the z-test adequate.

Shared parent runs correlate decisions: a parent that was unlucky on its pool makes every candidate look better. This adds confirmations but does not inflate the per-test rate; Bonferroni covers the dependence, and panels are refreshed after 4 uses.
The simulated counts assume stationary, additive effects, so they are upper bounds: after acceptances the remaining improvements get rarer and effects stop adding.
The min(acquired, gain) statistic rejects edits that raise the untrained score as much as the acquired one. This is deliberate (instruction 6.2) and costs acceptances.

Bin packing's paired sd and the held-out categories' CPU per run are unmeasured. If bin packing's paired sd exceeds 0.01, its share of the panel grows. If held-out runs average more than 10 CPU-s, the held-out generation test shrinks first (pre-registered order).
Equal weights give p-median a third of the estimand although design o gains about 0 there, which dilutes learning-principle edits.
measure() scores training instances outside its CPU fields (kernel/run.py, after cpu_apply), so machine time exceeds charged CPU by ~10-20%. The budget keeps a reserve for this.
A better measurement cannot create positive principle edits, only find them if they exist. Principle cells screened mostly harmful (propose/replace -0.040, init/mutarg -0.020).
novelty:
None of the statistics is new: Wald's sequential probability ratio test, racing for algorithm configuration (Hoeffding races, F-Race, successive halving), Neyman allocation, common random numbers, pooled variance with empirical-Bayes shrinkage, Bonferroni bounds, and random-effects reasoning about transfer.

What is new relative to design o:
- Its step allocated seeds per category regardless of noise and cost.
- It spent half its CPU on a category with no signal.
- It accepted on a t over heterogeneous pairs with 15 df.
- It fed one-seed screens to the discoverer.
- It accepted on a different statistic (change of acquired) from its held-out endpoint (min of the acquired and gain changes).
This technique replaces all of that. It also adds a confirmation category that no selection saw, a per-step transfer endpoint, and a generation-quality version of the swap test.

Relative to design q: q moves the representation search inside acquisition and is starved by the same noise. This technique is orthogonal (an outer measurement) and could serve q's discovery unchanged.

It is not a new learning principle and does not make one more likely to exist. It makes one detectable at about 0.004 instead of 0.018, and it turns a negative answer into a measured bound.
implementation_plan:
About 1,350 lines, about one day. Every step runs on source categories only, on scratch ledgers, until registration.

1. Free ledger analyses, no CPU (diagnose_r.py, ~120 lines).
   - rho-hat from the off-diagonal covariances of design o's per-category screening values (jobshop, quadassign, pmedian), over all 142 non-zero candidates and over candidates of pre-declared mild cells. Selecting by cell rather than by value keeps the covariances unbiased.
   - Paired sd per category and per parent.
   - CPU per run.
2. acceptance.py (~300 lines) and test_acceptance.py (~150 lines).
   - Null calibration by resampling design o's centred confirmation pairs: must give <= 0.006 per confirmation and <= 0.05 per lineage.
   - An injected +0.006 effect must be accepted >= 70% of the time.
   - Neyman arithmetic and replay identity.
3. Development panel (~1,600 CPU-s). o0, batch 6 and holdback 0.3 on quadassign, jobshop, pmedian and binpacking, 12 seeds each, at the search budget. This gives bin packing's paired sd and the per-category CPU, which fix CYCLE and the panel through the formula.
4. discovery_r.py (~280 lines) and experiment_r.py (~300 lines). Dev run of every stage with budgets divided by 20 (~900 CPU-s), held-out replaced by source categories as experiment_q does; stop-and-resume replay check.
5. Apply the budget rule when budget_scaling.json lands. Write registration_r.json with every constant, the file hashes and the predictions. Independent review before the registered run.
compute_budget:
Counted CPU as the kernel records it, against the 300,000 available.

| stage | CPU-s |
|---|---|
| Development (before registration, source categories; ~600 h on top of the day's runs is not involved, see note) | ~2,500 |
| Discovery: 3 arms x 3 lineages x 18,000 charged | 162,000 |
| Selection | ~2,000 |
| Generation test (only if E3(a) holds; 0 otherwise) | 30,000 |
| Held-out stage (assumes <= 10 CPU-s per run) | ~34,000 |
| Total counted | 198,000-228,000 |

Notes:
- Development breakdown: ledger analyses 0, development panel 1,600, dev lineage at 1/20 budget 900, calibrations under 10.
- Discovery uses less machine time than it is charged: R and F share every run until the first accepted change of principle, and all lineages share generation 0's race pool through the cache.
- Held-out stage breakdown: finals, other lineages, o0 and a0 at 12 seeds, 5,300; matched controls for o0, a0, F and T, ~6,000; M3 accepted steps, ~7,500 (capped at 40 steps); held-out generation test, ~15,000.
- Machine time: about 1.15x counted, because the kernel scores training instances outside its CPU fields, so 228,000-262,000. That leaves at least 38,000 in reserve for unknown held-out run costs and re-runs.
